To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
hnRNPs A1 and A/B2 function to maintain the length of telomeres in cells expressing telomerase.

(i) hnRNP A/B proteins play an important role in the maintenance of telomeres in cells that express telomerase (cancer cells), but not in telomerase-negative cells; and (ii) hnRNP-A/B-mediated telomere maintenance requires telomerase activity.
hnRNP proteins A1 and A are required for telomerase-dependent telomere maintenance in cancer cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of the molecular mechanisms that regulate telomerase function in normal and cancer cells, which may provide novel therapeutic strategies for cancer treatment.
the identification of novel factors required for the maintenance of telomeres in human cancer cells.
the role of hnRNPs in telomere maintenance and the regulation of cell proliferation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the simultaneous depletion of hnRnPA1/A2 results in the inhibition of cell growth in telomerase-positive cancer cells, which is due to dysfunctional telomeres.

the simultaneous depletion of hnRnpA1/A2 results in telomere shortening in cancer cells, and the telomere shortness is a result of the loss of the function of hnRnp A1 and A1, and that the telomere length in normal cells is not affected by hnRnp A/B depletion.
the hnRNPs A/B play a role in telomere maintenance and that this is a telomerase-dependent process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the simultaneous suppression hnRNP A/B subfamily hnRNPs, which are essential for cell proliferation, induces apoptosis in cancer cells by inducing dysfunctional telomeres, but not in normal cells.
hnRNP-A1 and A2 are required for maintaining telomerase activity and functional telomeres.
hnRNP-A/B is a novel regulator for telomerase-dependent telomere maintenance.

hnRNPs A1 and A1 function to maintain telomerases in telomerase expressing cells.
